items.title: Boot a personal PS2 homebrew ELF from PCSX2
items.summary: Use the documented `-elf` override to test a lawful homebrew executable separately from a disc image and ordinary library launch.

items.title: Check PCSX2 configuration before booting a game
items.summary: Run the documented `-testconfig` startup check to initialize and check the PCSX2 configuration version without opening a game.

items.title: Compare full BIOS boot and fast boot after a PS2 startup error
items.summary: Run paired cold launches with the same BIOS, image, and card to see whether a startup fault changes when the normal firmware sequence is skipped.

items.title: Set the right Multitap port for a four-player PS2 game
items.summary: Map a four-player PS2 session by checking which console port the game expects, assigning emulator slots in order, and testing every seat before loading a long match.

items.title: Isolate PCSX2 crashes linked to EZFRD64.dll controller drivers
items.summary: Use a controlled unplug test to verify whether a legacy controller driver is implicated before removing it.

items.title: Enable DualShock 4 enhanced mode without changing your mappings
items.summary: Use SDL and enhanced mode only for a supported official controller, then test LEDs and vibration separately.

items.title: Launch a PS2 image with spaces or a leading dash in its filename
items.summary: Use PCSX2’s `--` delimiter so the remaining command-line text is treated as the boot filename, including spaces or a leading dash.

items.title: Launch PCSX2 directly into Big Picture mode
items.summary: Use the official `-bigpicture` option when building a controller-only PCSX2 launch shortcut, and verify the interface separately from game boot.

items.title: Make a PS2 Buzz controller appear in PCSX2 on Windows
items.summary: Identify the Buzz receiver in Device Manager and select Windows USB Input Device only for that receiver when it is absent from PCSX2.

items.title: Remap a misreported controller with SDL Raw Input on Windows
items.summary: Use SDL Raw Input as a Windows fallback when a third-party pad reports scrambled or unresponsive controls, and map each physical input manually.

items.title: Add a second input to one PS2 button safely
items.summary: Use the Shift-click mapping menu to let a controller and keyboard activate the same emulated button, then test and remove only the added binding if needed.

items.title: Map a PS2 mouse pointer and keep control of the emulator
items.summary: Enable pointer input only for a mouse-driven PS2 title, map the required buttons, test cursor capture safely, and keep a reliable route back to emulator controls.

items.title: Open the PS2 system menu for a BIOS boot check
items.summary: Use the documented `-bios` option to start the BIOS system menu, then distinguish a firmware boot result from launching a game image.

items.title: Rerun the PCSX2 setup wizard from a copied launcher
items.summary: Use `-setupwizard` to force the documented initial setup wizard, while preserving a backup and the ordinary shortcut for a safe comparison.

items.title: Run a PCSX2 batch launch test without the main window
items.summary: Use `-batch` or `-nogui` for a controlled automation test, remembering that `-nogui` implies batch mode and may exit when emulation shuts down.

items.title: Choose where PCSX2 stores portable data from the command line
items.summary: Compare PCSX2’s `-portable` and `-datapath` switches in a temporary launch, noting that `-portable` takes precedence over `-datapath`.

items.title: Start a short PCSX2 test in turbo mode
items.summary: Use the documented `-turbo` launch option only for a brief controlled check, then return to normal-speed play before evaluating timing or performance.

items.title: Stop Steam Input from triggering PCSX2 hotkeys during play
items.summary: Isolate controller events from Steam’s desktop layout, then verify that buttons reach the PS2 game without opening the emulator menu or pausing unexpectedly.

items.title: Validate PS2 controller mappings with the PCSX2 Pad Test
items.summary: Use the Pad Test homebrew linked from PCSX2 documentation to check mapped DualShock 2 inputs independently from a game.

items.title: Capture a separate PCSX2 log for a launch test
items.summary: Use `-logfile` to direct one PCSX2 launch’s log to a dedicated file, then verify the file before sharing diagnostics.

items.title: Check RetroAchievements Hardcore before a long gaming session
items.summary: Confirm game recognition, the active mode and recorded achievement progress. Keep normal saves safe and follow the client’s restrictions.

items.title: Choose ASTC texture quality in EmuCoreX
items.summary: Keep the original texture archive, compare one scene at different block sizes and check that conversion finishes successfully before evaluating the result.

items.title: Restore selected EmuCoreX data from Google Drive safely
items.summary: Check the Drive account, backup date and selected categories. Keep a separate recovery copy, then verify progress using a normal in-game save.

items.title: Hide and show library entries without deleting game files
items.summary: Hide distracting entries from the library and use the hidden list to show them again. The game files and saves remain on the device.

items.title: Verify a CHD before replacing the original disc image
items.summary: Check the container and transfer without modifying the files. Keep the original disc dump until integrity checks and a gameplay test both succeed.

items.title: Install, test, and roll back a custom Android GPU driver
items.summary: Use custom AdrenoTools-compatible drivers only on supported Adreno hardware, record a system-driver baseline, verify the package, test one variable, and keep an immediate rollback path.

items.title: Match the renderer to the Android GPU and driver
items.summary: Identify the real SoC and GPU, distinguish Adreno from Mali and other families, test API support, and choose a renderer based on the device's driver rather than marketing names.

items.title: Manage heat, throttling, battery, storage speed, and long-session stability
items.summary: Measure sustained rather than launch performance, control brightness and charging heat, detect thermal throttling, validate storage behaviour, and build a conservative profile for long PS2 sessions.

items.title: Find duplicate PS2 images with SHA-256 before deleting anything
items.summary: Create a read-only hash inventory on Windows, Linux, or macOS; group byte-identical personal disc images; distinguish active copies from offline backups; and remove only verified redundancy from scanned folders.

items.title: Restore EmuCoreX library access after an Android update
items.summary: Reconnect the exact PS2 library tree through Android's Storage Access Framework, distinguish a revoked permission from a missing SD card, avoid duplicate roots, and prove that access survives a reboot before removing anything.

Access documents and other files from shared storage

items.title: Export EmuCoreX per-game profiles before a tuning session
items.summary: Use the Per-Game Settings Manager's JSON export as a versioned snapshot, verify which profiles it contains, tune one title, and understand that importing a snapshot replaces the complete profile collection.

items.title: Quarantine new personal PS2 dumps before EmuCoreX scans them
items.summary: Use an unscanned intake area to finish dump verification, remove partial files, validate CD track sets, record serials and hashes, and promote only accepted working copies into the playable library.

items.title: Build a repeatable PS2 graphics regression test scene
items.summary: Create a legal in-game checkpoint with fixed camera, inputs, settings, expected artifacts, timing window, and clean-save recovery so renderer, driver, and emulator updates can be judged against the same workload.

items.title: Build a per-game controller profile
items.summary: Preserve a known-good shared mapping, create one explicitly named game override, document its differences, assign it only to the intended title, and test isolation.

items.title: Build a per-game PS2 performance budget
items.summary: Define target emulation speed, frame-time reserve, thermal duration, resolution, accuracy, and battery conditions for one title, then accept a profile only when its worst known scenes remain inside the recorded limits.

items.title: Build a touchscreen layout for portrait testing
items.summary: Create a separate portrait diagnostic layout, respect cutout and gesture insets, preserve the PS2 viewport, test combinations, and prove rotation does not overwrite landscape.

items.title: Calibrate analog-stick dead zones for PS2 games
items.summary: Measure neutral drift and full circular travel, raise the inner dead zone only above observed noise, verify fine movement and maximum range in two game contexts, then repeat after controller reconnect.

items.title: Calibrate analog trigger range for PS2 input
items.summary: Observe released, partial, and fully pressed L2 and R2 values, remove duplicate digital bindings, set only the minimum supported threshold needed, and prove gradual travel plus full activation after reconnect.

items.title: Capture a minimal PCSX2 GS dump for a rendering report
items.summary: Reproduce a graphics fault on desktop PCSX2, capture only the necessary GS command window, replay it locally, record renderer and serial metadata, and share no disc image, firmware, or unrelated gameplay.

items.title: Capture useful before-and-after graphics evidence
items.summary: Match serial, camera, animation frame, renderer, driver, resolution, and one tested variable; keep lossless captures with readable metadata and reject pairs whose timing, crop, color pipeline, or game state changed.

items.title: Check FAT32 limits before copying large PS2 DVD images
items.summary: Identify the destination filesystem, find every image near or above 4 GiB, run one large-file copy and hash test, and choose a supported storage format before committing an EmuCoreX library migration.

items.title: Choose texture filtering for 2D-heavy PS2 games
items.summary: Compare fonts, sprites, pixel-art menus, and 3D backgrounds at native output, determine which elements the game expects to be filtered, and keep a per-game choice that avoids both blur and atlas bleeding.

items.title: Combine controller and touchscreen inputs
items.summary: Assign clear ownership between a physical controller and touch overlay, expose only missing functions, and test switching, simultaneous input, reconnect, and neutral release.

items.title: Compare plugged-in and battery PS2 performance safely
items.summary: Separate charging heat from power-source policy by comparing matched routes, battery ranges, cable states, and temperature checkpoints without cycling a hot phone repeatedly or treating a brief turbo result as sustained performance.

sources.title: Monitor the battery level and charging state

items.title: Compare Vulkan and OpenGL on one PS2 title
items.summary: Hold resolution, accuracy, driver, and scene fixed while measuring cold startup, warm frame pacing, graphics correctness, readbacks, and lifecycle stability on each API, then keep a per-game result backed by repeatable evidence.

items.title: Configure a dance mat, wheel, or arcade stick for one PS2 title
items.summary: Identify the title's expected peripheral, test Android events, build one scoped dance-mat, wheel, or arcade profile, and verify simultaneous input and safe feedback behavior.

items.title: Configure alternatives for pressure-sensitive PS2 buttons
items.summary: Identify a title's pressure-sensitive action, confirm controller limits, map a deliberate pressure modifier or alternate control, and verify light versus full behavior.

items.title: Correct depth fighting without confusing it with frame-pacing flicker
items.summary: Freeze one camera where two surfaces alternate, prove the conflict in captured frames, compare native software and hardware output, then test only a documented depth-related correction while protecting decals and shadows.

items.title: Correct a half-screen or offset PS2 post-processing pass
items.summary: Verify that bloom, blur, depth-of-field, or color grading aligns at native resolution, identify the exact upscale multiplier that displaces it, and apply only a documented coordinate or sprite correction to the affected title.

sources.title: Explanation: Hacks Needed for Upscaling Glitches

items.title: Correct interlaced combing by testing motion and field order
items.summary: Record a repeatable lateral pan, inspect individual fields, compare supported deinterlacing modes one at a time, and select the mode that removes serrated motion without trading it for bobbing or blur.

items.title: Keep a read-only PS2 preservation master and a separate working copy
items.summary: Freeze a verified personal dump with logs and hashes outside EmuCoreX scans, derive a replaceable working copy for names and external patches, and rehearse rebuilding that copy without modifying the master.

items.title: Create a reproducible PS2 emulation performance report
items.summary: Package device and software identity, game serial and hash, exact settings, normal save, timed route, cold and warm results, logs, screenshots, expected behavior, and one-variable comparisons into a report another tester can replay.

items.title: Detect thermal throttling during long PS2 sessions
items.summary: Correlate a gradual speed decline with elapsed heat, thermal status, and controlled changes such as lower resolution or removing an insulating case, while avoiding unsafe cooling and misleading scene changes.

items.title: Diagnose a controller that works in Android but not a game
items.summary: Locate the layer where controller input stops by comparing Android navigation, emulator hotkeys, a PS2 pad test, and the target game's expected port or mode.

items.title: Diagnose a missing left or right PS2 audio channel
items.summary: Use a stereo control clip, a second PS2 title, route swaps, and earpiece reversal to locate one missing channel without masking it with mono output.

items.title: Diagnose a PS2 image that appears under the wrong library title
items.summary: Compare detected serial, physical-disc record, dump log, executable region, filename, hash, and metadata source to decide whether the fault belongs to presentation, identity, or the working image.

items.title: Diagnose a renderer crash during shader compilation
items.summary: Distinguish expected first-run shader work from a repeatable driver crash by comparing cold and warm launches, restoring the system driver, changing one API, and preserving the exact scene and log that triggers compilation.

items.title: Diagnose a stuck button or axis
items.summary: Observe the exact held value, separate analog drift from missing release or duplicate bindings, test each source alone, and verify neutral state across lifecycle interruptions.

items.title: Diagnose a black PS2 FMV when its audio continues
items.summary: Reproduce one exact cutscene from a full boot, prove whether decoded video reaches software output, check the disc image independently, and separate IPU, renderer, field-order, and stale-state failures.

items.title: Diagnose Bluetooth controller latency
items.summary: Use a repeatable input event, local display, and comparison connection to distinguish Bluetooth controller delay from frame pacing, audio routing, or radio interference.

items.title: Diagnose controller buttons that activate twice
items.summary: Use a neutral input display to distinguish duplicate emulator bindings, two Android device interfaces, turbo mode, accessibility actions, and game repeat behavior, changing one layer until one press creates one transition.

items.title: Diagnose corrupted PS2 skyboxes across camera angles and cold boots
items.summary: Separate a bad sky texture from depth ordering, stale graphics cache, upscaling, and driver behavior by recording a panoramic route at native output and changing one disposable layer at a time.

items.title: Diagnose distorted or clipped PS2 audio
items.summary: Compare loud and quiet passages at safe volume, correlate artifacts with speed and route, bypass processing, and change buffering only when evidence indicates underruns.

items.title: Diagnose frame pacing on a 120 Hz phone
items.summary: Compare fixed 60 Hz and 120 Hz at full emulation speed, separate recurring cadence from event-based stutter, and verify the chosen mode over a sustained thermal pass.

items.title: Diagnose geometry that vanishes near widescreen edges
items.summary: Use an edge-panning route to distinguish widescreen culling from clipping, renderer loss, and ordinary draw distance; compare unpatched 4:3, serial-matched 16:9, and fixed-camera scenes before keeping a patch.

items.title: Separate PS2 motion ghosting from deinterlacing and upscaling artifacts
items.summary: Record motion at native resolution, compare fields and static frames, disable post-processing, test deinterlacing independently, and preserve intentional trails while removing duplicated character edges introduced by the output path.

sources.title: Explanation: Hacks Needed for Upscaling Glitches

items.title: Diagnose memory pressure and unexpected PS2 emulator restarts
items.summary: Separate a true process restart from a game crash or activity recreation by preserving logs, watching memory growth, testing texture and capture features independently, and reproducing under a fixed Android workload.

items.title: Restore missing fog and haze with a software-rendered reference
items.summary: Choose two depth-rich scenes, compare native hardware APIs with a short software reference, increase framebuffer or blending accuracy minimally, and verify that restored haze does not cover the HUD or flatten scene depth.

items.title: Diagnose missing music with working sound effects
items.summary: Verify the game scene and music option, cold-boot without save state, compare disc integrity and another title, and avoid global audio changes when effects already work.

items.title: Diagnose missing particles and per-pixel alpha effects
items.summary: Use a repeatable smoke, sparks, rain, or energy effect to separate missing draws from incorrect per-pixel alpha blending, compare software and hardware paths, and retain the least expensive correction that preserves layer order.

items.title: Diagnose missing shadows without stacking graphics hacks
items.summary: Capture one shadow-heavy scene at native resolution, identify whether the absent layer is geometry, depth, or blending, compare hardware APIs and a software reference, then retain only the smallest per-game correction.

items.title: Distinguish first-run shader stutter from recurring frame-time hitches
items.summary: Run a fixed route cold and warm without deleting cache, mark every hitch location, and classify only first-visit pauses as compilation candidates while preserving recurring I/O, scene, or lifecycle stalls for separate diagnosis.

items.title: Diagnose a PS2 picture that shakes or jitters vertically
items.summary: Measure whether motion affects the entire frame or only interlaced edges, compare menus with gameplay, control output refresh and video-mode changes, and reject fixes that merely blur the oscillation.

items.title: Diagnose slow FMV playback when PS2 gameplay runs normally
items.summary: Compare one reproducible cutscene with nearby gameplay, verify emulation speed and audio drift, separate video decode or IPU behavior from general rendering load, and capture evidence without applying broad speed changes.

items.title: Diagnose slow PS2 gameplay when menus remain full speed
items.summary: Compare menu, lightweight gameplay, and one heavy scene with matched counters to identify whether the workload scales with game logic, geometry, effects, or resolution instead of using menu speed as proof of compatibility.

items.title: Diagnose storage-induced loading stutter in PS2 games
items.summary: Correlate pauses with disc reads, area transitions, cache misses, and Android storage location by replaying one loading boundary from internal and removable storage while preserving image identity and emulator settings.

items.title: Diagnose texture-cache corruption after a renderer crash
items.summary: Distinguish stale disposable graphics data from damaged game files or saves by restarting Android, reproducing on the system driver, rebuilding only documented cache once, and proving later cold launches remain clean.

items.title: Diagnose vertical seams that appear only after PS2 upscaling
items.summary: Map the first resolution multiplier that exposes the seams, distinguish sprite alignment from texture-atlas bleeding, and keep only a documented per-game correction that leaves HUD and geometry intact.

items.title: Distinguish CPU bottlenecks from GPU bottlenecks in PS2 emulation
items.summary: Use one fixed scene, native and higher internal resolution, emulation speed, frame time, and PCSX2-style GS counters to identify which workload responds to GPU changes and which remains limited by emulated CPU work.

items.title: Build a device-neutral PS2 library restoration manifest
items.summary: Record titles, serials, regions, revisions, disc relationships, relative paths, bytes, SHA-256, storage roles, and verification dates so another Android device can reconstruct roots without copying stale URIs.

items.title: Fix audio crackle, latency, and synchronization problems
items.summary: Separate underruns caused by low emulation speed from output-latency problems, test a stable buffer, and avoid hiding timing faults with asynchronous audio modes.

items.title: Diagnose black screens, crashes, freezes, and renderer faults with logs
items.summary: Reproduce one failure from a clean baseline, separate bad dumps from renderer and core faults, preserve the right log before relaunching, and build a report others can repeat.

items.title: Set up EmuCoreX safely on the first run
items.summary: A clean first-run path for Android: choose the safe profile, identify the GPU family, connect a personal BIOS dump, grant durable folder access, and confirm one game before changing advanced settings.

items.title: Set internal resolution for phones, tablets, handhelds, and TVs
items.summary: Choose an internal resolution from screen density and sustained GPU headroom, test it with a fixed scene, and avoid wasting heat on pixels the display or game cannot reveal.

items.title: Organize storage and scan a PS2 library
items.summary: Build a predictable Android folder layout, grant durable access, scan multiple locations without duplicates, and recover from moved folders or removable-storage failures.

items.title: Create, audit, and reset per-game profiles
items.summary: Keep global defaults clean, store only justified game-specific overrides, record the problem each solves, and reset a profile without disturbing saves or other titles.

items.title: Build a performance profile without unsafe speed-hack stacking
items.summary: Find the real bottleneck, change one control per test, separate global and per-game settings, and preserve a reversible Safe baseline instead of piling hacks together.

items.title: Map a physical controller, pressure buttons, and rumble
items.summary: Create a clean DualShock 2 mapping, calibrate sticks, handle pressure-sensitive actions deliberately, verify rumble routing, and recover from doubled Android inputs.

items.title: Choose Vulkan, OpenGL, or software rendering
items.summary: Select a renderer by evidence: establish a safe Vulkan or OpenGL baseline, recognize device-specific faults, use software rendering as a diagnostic, and roll back without stacking fixes.

items.title: Use save states safely without replacing in-game saves
items.summary: Treat save states as version-sensitive checkpoints, keep memory-card saves authoritative, avoid cross-profile timeline conflicts, and recover cleanly when a state no longer loads.

items.title: Install and troubleshoot PS2 texture replacements
items.summary: Match a texture pack to the exact title and dump naming, keep replacements outside the game image, control memory pressure, and isolate missing or incorrect textures with logging.

items.title: Create a usable touchscreen control layout
items.summary: Design touch controls around reach, visibility, simultaneous actions, pressure needs, and repeatable gameplay tests instead of shrinking a full DualShock 2 onto the display.

items.title: Evaluate a phone cooling accessory safely for PS2 emulation
items.summary: Compare passive baseline and accessory-assisted sustained routes at matched temperature, power, case, and fan settings, recording time-to-throttle and stability while avoiding condensation, blocked vents, and unsafe charging combinations.

items.title: Diagnose a PS2 game that renders the HUD but not the world
items.summary: Use the surviving HUD as evidence that presentation is active, verify the disc image, reset draw-disabling overrides, compare hardware APIs and a short software reference, then capture the smallest reproducible world-geometry failure.

items.title: Remove color banding introduced by a post-processing shader
items.summary: Capture one smooth sky or fog gradient with post-processing disabled, re-enable shader stages individually, inspect output before display conversion, and keep only a preset whose precision does not crush or posterize the source.

items.title: Fix swapped or inverted analog axes
items.summary: Trace a wrong stick direction through the Android axis event, the saved PS2 binding, and the game's own camera options, then correct exactly one reversed or exchanged axis and verify the full circle.

items.title: Repair transparent PS2 effects that render as solid surfaces
items.summary: Use a repeatable glass, water, smoke, or menu overlay to distinguish missing alpha blending from texture or draw-order faults, increase accuracy one step at a time, and test unrelated translucent layers before saving the override.

items.title: Restore broken bloom in hardware rendering without overexposing the scene
items.summary: Use paired bright and dark checkpoints to identify a missing or misaligned framebuffer pass, compare a software reference, and find the least expensive blending or native-scaling correction.

items.title: Organize multidisc PS2 games without losing disc order or region
items.summary: Verify each owned disc independently, record serial and hash relationships, adopt explicit Disc 1/Disc 2 names, test the game's real swap or save handoff, and roll back the complete set together.

items.title: Identify anamorphic widescreen versus letterboxed PS2 output
items.summary: Use circles, character proportions, 2D overlays, and FMV boundaries to determine whether a title renders true anamorphic 16:9, embeds a letterbox inside 4:3, or needs separate aspect handling for gameplay and video.
